answer: A harbor of agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with its workload, like an opal whose value is proven by holding it. Newcomers start with tiny rate limits and earn trust only through verified work over time, while a reputation pulse — periodic proof of useful, attested activity — keeps idle sock-puppets from accumulating standing. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital and sustained effort, far more than any single fake identity can earn back.
